summary: Michael Janda is a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of Vienna and his Habilitation at the University of Zurich. He held an assistant post at Zurich in 1995 and a chair at Münster in 2002.

Michael Jansen (1947–2022) was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Bonn, Sapienza, Delhi, the Archaeological Survey of India, and RWTH Aachen. He served as dean of architecture at RWTH Aachen (1988–1999) and founding rector at GUtech (2007–2008).

Michael Jay Sweet (d. 2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD under Geshe Lhundub Sopa at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he was attested as a clinical assistant professor in psychiatry in 1996 and 2006.

Michael Jerryson (1974–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and earned his PhD under Mark Juergensmeyer at UC Santa Barbara, later holding professorial posts at Eckerd College and Youngstown State University.
Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in Tibetology. He studied at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter is a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Larry William Moses. He served as a research fellow at the Lumbini International Research Institute and as a cataloger at Indiana University Bloomington.
Michael M. Broido is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge and held a post at the University of Oxford.
Michael Oppitz is a scholar of Tibetology. He held a post at the Institute for Advanced Study, Berlin (~1987–1988) and served as director at the University of Zurich (~1991–2008).
Michael P. Berman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 2012, he was attested as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies.

Michael Puett is a sinologist, historian, and philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu. He has held professorships in humanities, Chinese history, and anthropology at Harvard University since approximately 1994.

Michael Pye is a scholar of religious, Buddhist, and Japanese studies who earned degrees from Cambridge and Leeds. He held teaching posts at Leeds and Lancaster, a professorship at the University of Marburg (1982–2004), and a visiting professorship at Otani University.

Michael Radich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Harvard. He held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and Kyoto University, and became professor of Buddhist studies at Heidelberg University in 2018.
Michael S. Drummond is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was attested as a PhD candidate at Utrecht University in 2006.

Michael Schmidt is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 1981, 2008), the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (1992), and the University of Göttingen (attested 1995).

Michael Sheehy is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at CIIS under Steven D. Goodman. He held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia (attested 2019–2026).

Michael Silverstein (1945–2020) was a linguist who studied at Harvard University (~1961–1972) after attending Stuyvesant High School. He held a post at the University of Chicago from around 1970 to 2020.

Michael Stanley-Baker is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned an MA under Stephen R. Bokenkamp at Indiana University Bloomington. He has held posts at the MPIWG, Leipzig University, University of Pittsburgh, and Nanyang Technological University.
Michael Torsten Much is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He was a fellow at the University of Hamburg and studied under Ernst Steinkellner (attested 1991).

Michael Viggo Fausbøll (1821–1908) was a Danish Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at the University of Copenhagen under Niels Ludvig Westergaard, he served there as an assistant librarian in 1861 and as professor of Indian philology from 1878 to 1902.

Michael W. Meister is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who earned his BA, MA, and PhD from Harvard University and studied at the University of Pennsylvania. In 1976, he became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania, succeeding Stella Kramrisch.
